examples.cn: 酒店员工礼貌而反应及时。

examples.en: Her illness proved responsive to treatment.
examples.cn: 她的病对治疗有良好反应。

examples.en: The app uses a responsive layout on tablets.
examples.cn: 这个应用在平板上采用响应式布局。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「response + ive」——随时能「回应」的，就是反应灵敏的；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ spondere（承诺）→ respondere（回以答复）→ response ＋ -ive → responsive，核心义「随时作出回应的」。

sensesIntro.en: Responsive first means quick to react, then reacting well to treatment, and finally reacting to technical input.
sensesIntro.cn: responsive 先指反应迅速，再指对治疗反应良好，最后指对技术输入作出响应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an instant answer to a touch or call.
core.cn: 核心意象：对触碰或呼叫的即时回答。

branches.en: Quick reaction is the core sense.
branches.cn: 迅速反应是核心义项。

branches.en: A good reaction to treatment is the medical sense.
branches.cn: 对治疗的良好反应是医学义项。

branches.en: Reacting to input is the technical sense.
branches.cn: 对输入作出反应是技术义项。

branches.en: Both a help desk and a patient can answer well.
branches.cn: 服务台与病人都能作出良好回应。

branches.en: A responsive screen answers every touch at once.
branches.cn: 响应式屏幕对每次触摸都立即回答。

intro.en: Responsive is a Latin answering word with the English adjective suffix -ive.
intro.cn: responsive 是拉丁语「答复」词加上英语形容词词尾 -ive。

latinIntro.en: Latin respondere means to answer in return, from spondere, to promise.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 respondere 意为回以答复，源于 spondere（承诺）。

items.exampleCN: responsiveness 指迅速反应的能力。

definition_zh: 休息；剩余部分；依靠；停止
definition_en: to relax, the part that remains, or to be supported by something
core_image: 一个人放下工具，靠在树边歇一口气
scene: 走了很远之后，大家在树荫下休息。After a long walk, everyone rested in the shade.
sceneCN: 这里 rested 是 rest 的过去式，表示「休息」（第 2 个义项：停止活动以恢复体力）；句意：走了很远之后，大家在树荫下休息。

senses.title: The part that remains
senses.definition: the people or things that are left after the others are taken
senses.definitionCN: 其他人或事物被拿走之后剩下的部分
senses.example: I ate one apple and kept the rest.
senses.exampleCN: 我吃了一个苹果，把其余的留着。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different root meaning to remain, and it names what is left behind.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个意为「留下」的词根，指被留下的东西。

senses.title: A period of relaxation
senses.definition: a period of time spent relaxing or not working
senses.definitionCN: 用于放松或不工作的一段时间
senses.example: You look tired and need a good rest.
senses.exampleCN: 你看起来很累，需要好好休息。
senses.why: The oldest English sense is bodily rest, a pause from effort.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的英语义项是身体休息，即从劳作中暂停。

senses.title: To relax or stop activity
senses.definition: to stop working or moving in order to recover
senses.definitionCN: 停止工作或移动以恢复体力
senses.example: Let us rest here for a few minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在这里休息几分钟吧。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun of relaxation into an action.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「休息」这一名词转化为动作。

senses.title: To be supported or based on
senses.definition: to be supported by something or to depend on it
senses.definitionCN: 由某物支撑或依赖某物
senses.example: The whole plan rests on one assumption.
senses.exampleCN: 整个计划建立在一个假设之上。
senses.why: Something at rest on a support is held up by it, which gives the sense of depending.
senses.whyCN: 静止在某支撑物上的东西由它托住，因此产生「依赖」的含义。

intro.en: Rest has two sources: Old English ræst, a pause from work, and Old French reste, from Latin restare, to remain.
intro.cn: rest 有两个来源：古英语 ræst（停工歇息）与古法语 reste（源自拉丁语 restare，留下）。

items.en: Ræst means a pause, sleep, or resting place.
items.cn: ræst 意为暂停、睡眠或休息之处。

items.en: Restare means to remain or stand back.
items.cn: restare 意为留下、留在后面。

items.en: Reste means the remainder.
items.cn: reste 意为剩余部分。

items.en: Rest carries both the pause and the remainder senses.
items.cn: 中古英语 rest 同时带有「休息」与「剩余」两种含义。

items.en: Modern English adds rest on, meaning to depend on.
items.cn: 现代英语增加 rest on，表示依赖。

note.en: Rest is a double-rooted word, close to its restful and restless family and to words for breaks and remainders.
note.cn: rest 是双词源词，与 restful、restless 词族以及表示休息和剩余的词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Rest is two words in one coat: the pause from work and the part left over.
normalIntro.cn: rest 是穿着同一件外衣的两个词：从工作中暂停，以及剩下的部分。

normal.en: Take a rest means stop and relax for a while.
normal.cn: take a rest 表示停下来放松一会儿。

normal.en: The rest of the cake is in the fridge.
normal.cn: 剩下的蛋糕在冰箱里。

normal.en: A plan can rest on a single assumption.
normal.cn: 一个计划可能只建立在一个假设上。

normal.en: Restful places help you sleep well.
normal.cn: 宁静的地方有助于睡好。

normal.en: Compare break: a break is shorter, rest can be a longer state.
normal.cn: 对比 break：break 更短，rest 可以是更长的状态。

abstract.en: Picture a traveler setting down a heavy pack.
abstract.cn: 想象旅人放下沉重的背包。

abstract.en: Imagine a spoon resting across the rim of a cup.
abstract.cn: 想象一把勺子横搁在杯沿上。

abstract.en: Think of the last slice left on a plate.
abstract.cn: 想象盘子里剩下的最后一片。

examples.en: We walked for hours and then rested by the river.
examples.cn: 我们走了几个小时，然后在河边休息。

examples.en: She read the first page and skipped the rest.
examples.cn: 她读了第一页，其余部分跳过了。

examples.en: The argument rests on weak evidence.
examples.cn: 这个论点建立在薄弱的证据上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rest」——像人「靠」在椅子上歇一歇，也是剩下的部分；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ræst（歇息）＋ 古法语 reste（剩余，源自拉丁语 restare「留下」）→ 英语 rest，一身兼有「休息」与「剩余」两义。

sensesIntro.en: Rest first names what remains, then a pause for recovery, then the act of relaxing, and finally being supported by something.
sensesIntro.cn: rest 先指剩余之物，再指恢复体力的暂停，再指放松的动作，最后指由某物支撑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy pack set down and a body leaning back.
core.cn: 核心意象：沉重的背包被放下，身体向后靠。

branches.en: The remainder comes from the Latin remain root.
branches.cn: 剩余部分来自拉丁语「留下」词根。

branches.en: A pause for recovery comes from the Old English root.
branches.cn: 恢复体力的暂停来自古英语词根。

branches.en: The verb of relaxing turns the pause into action.
branches.cn: 休息的动词把暂停变为动作。

branches.en: Being supported links rest to reliance.
branches.cn: 被支撑把 rest 与依赖联系起来。

branches.en: Something at rest lies supported and still.
branches.cn: 静止之物躺在那儿，被支撑着不动。

intro.en: Rest has two roots, and its English family grows with -ful, -less, and -ing.
intro.cn: rest 有两个词根，其英语词族由 -ful、-less 与 -ing 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin restare means to remain, from re-, back, and stare, to stand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 restare 意为留下，由 re-（向后）与 stare（站立）构成。

items.example: Restless describes a need to move.
items.exampleCN: restless 描述想要走动的状态。

definition_en: a place where you pay to sit and eat meals
core_image: 一间亮着灯的店，里面摆着桌椅和热腾腾的饭菜
scene: 我们在一家小餐馆吃了热汤面。We had hot noodle soup at a small restaurant.
sceneCN: 这里 restaurant 是「餐馆」（第 1 个义项：供人付费用餐的场所）；句意：我们在一家小餐馆吃了热汤面。

senses.title: A place serving meals
senses.definition: a place where meals are cooked and served to paying customers
senses.definitionCN: 为付费顾客烹饪并提供饭菜的场所
senses.example: We found a quiet restaurant near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站附近找到一家安静的餐馆。
senses.why: French restaurant originally named a restoring broth, then the place that served it.
senses.whyCN: 法语 restaurant 最初指一种恢复体力的汤，后来指供应这种汤的地方。

senses.title: The business itself
senses.definition: the business or organization that runs such a place
senses.definitionCN: 经营这类场所的生意或组织
senses.example: The restaurant employs forty people.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐馆雇用了四十人。
senses.why: A restaurant can be spoken of as a business, not only as a building.
senses.whyCN: 餐馆不仅可以指建筑，也可以作为生意来谈论。

intro.en: Restaurant comes from French restaurer, to restore, because the first restaurants served a broth believed to restore health.
intro.cn: restaurant 来自法语 restaurer（恢复），因为最早的餐馆供应一种被认为能恢复健康的汤。

items.en: Restaurare means to restore or rebuild.
items.cn: restaurare 意为恢复、重建。

items.en: Restaurer means to restore.
items.cn: restaurer 意为恢复。

items.en: Restaurant first names a restoring broth.
items.cn: restaurant 最初指一种恢复体力的汤。

items.en: The word shifts to the place that serves food.
items.cn: 这个词转为指供应食物的场所。

items.en: English restaurant names a dining place.
items.cn: 英语 restaurant 指用餐场所。

items.en: Modern English uses it for all kinds of dining businesses.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指各类餐饮生意。

note.en: Restaurant is a dining-place word, close to its French-derived relatives and to other eating places.
note.cn: restaurant 是表示用餐场所的词，与法语来源的亲属词以及其他餐饮场所词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who often eats out
a small place serving drinks and light meals
an informal word for a restaurant

normalIntro.en: Restaurant began as a restoring broth: food that puts strength back into you.
normalIntro.cn: restaurant 最初是一种「恢复体力」的汤：让你重新有力气的食物。

normal.en: A restaurant serves meals for payment.
normal.cn: restaurant 为付费顾客提供饭菜。

normal.en: A restaurant owner is a restaurateur.
normal.cn: 餐馆老板是 restaurateur。

normal.en: A restaurant chain runs many branches.
normal.cn: restaurant chain 经营许多分店。

normal.en: Fast-food restaurants serve food quickly.
normal.cn: fast-food restaurant 快速供应食物。

normal.en: Compare café: a café is smaller and often serves drinks.
normal.cn: 对比 café：café 更小，常供应饮品。

abstract.en: Picture a warm window with tables and lamps inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇温暖的窗，里面摆着桌子和灯。

abstract.en: Imagine steam rising from a bowl of soup.
abstract.cn: 想象一碗汤冒着热气。

abstract.en: Think of a waiter carrying plates between tables.
abstract.cn: 想象服务员在桌间端着盘子穿行。

examples.en: The restaurant was full by seven o'clock.
examples.cn: 七点时餐馆已经坐满了。

examples.en: He works as a cook in a French restaurant.
examples.cn: 他在一家法国餐馆当厨师。

examples.en: They opened a second restaurant last spring.
examples.cn: 他们去年春天开了第二家餐馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rest + aurant」——进去「歇一歇」再吃顿饭，就是餐馆；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 restaurare（恢复）→ 法语 restaurer → restaurant（恢复体力的汤，后指供应食物的场所）→ 英语 restaurant，核心义「让人恢复精神的用餐处」。

sensesIntro.en: Restaurant first means the place that serves meals, and then the business that operates it.
sensesIntro.cn: restaurant 先指供应饭菜的场所，再指经营它的生意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit room where hot food restores tired people.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间亮着灯的房间，热饭让疲惫的人恢复精神。

branches.en: The dining place is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 用餐场所是日常义项。

branches.en: The business sense treats it as an enterprise.
branches.cn: 生意义项把它视为企业。

branches.en: A restaurant is both a room and a company.
branches.cn: 餐馆既是空间也是公司。

branches.en: A café, a diner, and a canteen can all be restaurants.
branches.cn: 咖啡馆、小饭馆与食堂都可以是餐馆。

branches.en: Chains and family restaurants differ in size, not in kind.
branches.cn: 连锁店与家庭餐馆规模不同，性质相同。

intro.en: Restaurant is a French restoring word, with English relatives restaurateur and restaurant-goer.
intro.cn: restaurant 是法语中表示「恢复」的词，英语亲属有 restaurateur 与 restaurant-goer。

latinIntro.en: Latin restaurare means to restore, and French restaurer keeps that sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 restaurare 意为恢复，法语 restaurer 保留这一含义。

items.example: Restaurer carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: restaurer 把这个词带入法语。
restaurant-goer 在 restaurant 后加 goer。

definition_zh: 焦躁不安的；无法安睡的；不停活动的
definition_en: unable to stay still or relax because of worry, excitement or boredom
core_image: 一只在笼中来回踱步、怎么也停不下来的动物
scene: 等待面试结果的整夜，他焦躁不安，反复起身走动。All night while waiting for the interview result, he was restless and kept getting up to walk around.
sceneCN: 这里 restless 是「焦躁不安的」（第 1 个义项：无法放松安静）；句意：等待面试结果的整夜，他焦躁不安，反复起身走动。

pos.zh: 焦躁不安的；无法安睡的；不停活动的

senses.title: Unable to stay calm
senses.definition: unable to relax or stay still because of worry or excitement
senses.definitionCN: 因担忧或兴奋而无法放松或安静下来
senses.example: The children grew restless before the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前孩子们变得焦躁不安。
senses.why: Restless literally means without rest, so the mind or body cannot settle.
senses.whyCN: restless 字面意为「没有休息」，所以身心都安定不下来。

senses.title: Without proper sleep
senses.definition: not giving or getting rest, especially sleep
senses.definitionCN: 不能让人休息，尤其是不能安睡
senses.example: She spent a restless night thinking about the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 她想着考试，辗转难眠了一整夜。
senses.why: A night without rest is restless because sleep never settles.
senses.whyCN: 没有休息的一夜之所以 restless，是因为睡眠始终没有安稳下来。

senses.title: Always moving
senses.definition: never still, moving about all the time
senses.definitionCN: 从不静止，总是动来动去
senses.example: A restless mind keeps turning over new ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 一颗不停运转的头脑总是翻来覆去地想着新点子。
senses.why: The same lack of rest can describe constant mental or physical motion.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「不得休息」也能形容思绪或身体持续不停的移动。

intro.en: Restless joins the Old English noun rest with the suffix -less, meaning without.
intro.cn: restless 由古英语名词 rest 加后缀 -less（没有）构成。

items.en: Ræst means a period of rest or sleep.
items.cn: ræst 意为休息或睡眠的一段时间。

items.en: The suffix -leas means without.
items.cn: 后缀 -leas 意为没有。

items.en: Restles describes a person who cannot be still.
items.cn: restles 形容无法安静的人。

items.en: Restless extends from sleeplessness to mental unease.
items.cn: restless 从失眠扩展到内心的不安。

items.en: Restless energy names motion that will not settle.
items.cn: restless energy 指无法安定的活动力。

note.en: Restless belongs to the family of rest and is close to words for unease.
note.cn: restless 属于 rest 词族，并与表示不安的词相近。

normalIntro.en: Restless is rest plus less: no rest at all, so the body keeps moving.
normalIntro.cn: restless 就是 rest 加 less：一点休息都没有，所以身体停不下来。

normal.en: A restless night is a night without real sleep.
normal.cn: a restless night 就是没有真正睡好的一夜。

normal.en: Children grow restless when they wait too long.
normal.cn: 孩子等得太久就会变得焦躁。

normal.en: Restless energy is power that will not sit still.
normal.cn: restless energy 是坐不住的精力。

normal.en: The adverb restlessly describes pacing up and down.
normal.cn: 副词 restlessly 描述来回踱步。

normal.en: Compare restful: restful calms you, restless will not let you calm down.
normal.cn: 对比 restful：restful 让你平静，restless 让你平静不下来。

abstract.en: Picture a pendulum that never stops swinging.
abstract.cn: 想象一只永不停摆的钟摆。

abstract.en: Imagine a page turning itself over again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸自己不停地翻来翻去。

abstract.en: Think of a chair that cannot hold anyone for long.
abstract.cn: 想象一把谁也坐不久的椅子。

examples.en: He felt restless and could not sit through the meeting.
examples.cn: 他坐立不安，无法把会开完。

examples.en: The baby was restless because of the heat.
examples.cn: 因为天气热，宝宝睡得很不安稳。

examples.en: Her restless fingers tapped the table all afternoon.
examples.cn: 一下午她的手指都不安分地敲着桌子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rest（休息）＋ less（少）」——休息太少，人就焦躁不安；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ræst（休息）＋ -leas（没有）→ restles → restless，核心义「得不到休息、安定不下来」。

sensesIntro.en: Restless starts with an unsettled mind, moves to broken sleep, and ends with constant motion.
sensesIntro.cn: restless 先指内心不安，再指睡眠不稳，最后指持续不停的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a caged animal pacing and never lying down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只在笼中来回踱步、从不躺下的动物。

branches.en: The basic sense is an unsettled, worried state.
branches.cn: 基本义是心神不宁、担忧的状态。

branches.en: Sleep offers no rest, so the night is broken.
branches.cn: 睡眠得不到休息，于是整夜断断续续。

branches.en: The body or mind never stops moving.
branches.cn: 身体或思绪从不停下。

branches.en: Worry at night produces both unease and poor sleep.
branches.cn: 夜里的担忧同时带来不安与失眠。

branches.en: Unease shows itself as pacing and fidgeting.
branches.cn: 不安会表现为踱步和坐立不安。

intro.en: Restless is a native English compound of a noun and a negative suffix.
intro.cn: restless 是由名词和否定后缀构成的英语本族复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here; the word grew inside Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，是在古英语内部形成的。

items.example: The suffix -ful gives the opposite feeling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 给出相反的感觉。

definition_en: to bring something back to an earlier or better condition
core_image: 工匠把一件破损的旧物一点点修补回原样
scene: 洪水退去后，村民们一起修复被冲毁的石桥。After the flood went down, the villagers worked together to restore the damaged stone bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 restore 是「修复」（第 2 个义项：把受损的建筑修回原状）；句意：洪水退去后，村民们一起修复被冲毁的石桥。

senses.title: Bring back a condition
senses.definition: to make something return to its former condition
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物回到原来的状态
senses.example: The new manager quickly restored calm in the office.
senses.exampleCN: 新经理很快恢复了办公室的平静。
senses.why: The Latin source means to rebuild, so restoring is putting a good state back.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为重建，因此 restore 就是让良好的状态重新回来。

senses.title: Repair something old
senses.definition: to repair an old building, painting or object so that it looks as it did
senses.definitionCN: 修理古老的建筑、画作或物品，使其恢复原貌
senses.example: Experts spent years restoring the ancient temple.
senses.exampleCN: 专家们花了多年时间修复这座古庙。
senses.why: Repairing an old thing is a physical way of giving it back its earlier state.
senses.whyCN: 修复旧物，是以实物的方式让它回到早先的状态。

senses.title: Give something back
senses.definition: to return something that was lost or taken
senses.definitionCN: 把丢失或被拿走的东西交还
senses.example: The police restored the stolen painting to its owner.
senses.exampleCN: 警方把被盗的画作归还给了失主。
senses.why: Returning an object puts it back where it belongs, which is another kind of restoring.
senses.whyCN: 把物品送还原处，是另一种意义上的恢复。

intro.en: Restore comes from Latin restaurare, to rebuild, through Old French restorer.
intro.cn: restore 经古法语 restorer 源自拉丁语 restaurare（重建）。

items.en: Restaurare means to rebuild or renew.
items.cn: restaurare 意为重建或更新。

items.en: The prefix re- adds the idea of again.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 增加「再次」的含义。

items.en: Restorer carries the meaning into French.
items.cn: restorer 把这一含义带入法语。

items.en: English restore covers repair and recovery.
items.cn: 英语 restore 涵盖修理与复原。

items.en: Restore now also means to give something back.
items.cn: 现代英语中 restore 还表示归还。

note.en: Restore is close to words for repairing and bringing back.
note.cn: restore 与表示修理和带回的词相近。

entries.definition: to return to a normal state

normalIntro.en: Restore is re- plus store: put the good condition back into store again.
normalIntro.cn: restore 是 re- 加 store：把良好的状态重新存回去。

normal.en: Restore order means bring calm back.
normal.cn: restore order 意为把秩序带回来。

normal.en: Restore a building means repair it carefully.
normal.cn: restore a building 意为仔细修好建筑。

normal.en: Restore power means make the lights work again.
normal.cn: restore power 意为让电灯重新亮起。

normal.en: The noun restoration names the whole repair process.
normal.cn: 名词 restoration 指整个修复过程。

normal.en: Compare repair: repair fixes damage, restore also brings back the original look.
normal.cn: 对比 repair：repair 修好损坏，restore 还恢复原貌。

abstract.en: Picture a cracked vase slowly becoming whole.
abstract.cn: 想象一只裂开的瓶子慢慢变得完整。

abstract.en: Imagine a switch bringing a dark street back to light.
abstract.cn: 想象一个开关让黑暗的街道重新亮起。

abstract.en: Think of an old photo cleaned until the faces return.
abstract.cn: 想象一张旧照片被擦净，人脸重新显现。

examples.en: The medicine helped restore her strength.
examples.cn: 这种药帮助她恢复了体力。

examples.en: Workers restored the old theater to its former beauty.
examples.cn: 工人们把老剧院修复到了昔日的美丽模样。

examples.en: He restored the borrowed book to the library shelf.
examples.cn: 他把借来的书放回了图书馆的书架。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）＋ store（存放）」——重新存回原来的样子，就是恢复与修复；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再）＋ restaurare（重建）→ 古法语 restorer → restore，核心义「让事物回到原来的良好状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Restore first means bring a condition back, then repair an old object, and finally return something to its owner.
sensesIntro.cn: restore 先指恢复状态，再指修复古物，最后指把东西归还原主。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a craftsman rebuilding a broken object piece by piece.
core.cn: 核心意象：工匠把破损的物件一块块重建起来。

branches.en: A condition is brought back to its earlier state.
branches.cn: 某种状态被带回早先的样子。

branches.en: An old building or artwork is repaired.
branches.cn: 古老的建筑或艺术品得到修复。

branches.en: A lost object is given back.
branches.cn: 丢失的物品被交还。

branches.en: Repairing an object also restores its lost value.
branches.cn: 修复物件也恢复了它失去的价值。

branches.en: Returning something restores the rightful order.
branches.cn: 归还原物恢复了应有的秩序。

intro.en: Restore is built from the Latin prefix re- and the rebuilding verb restaurare.
intro.cn: restore 由拉丁语前缀 re- 与表示重建的动词 restaurare 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin restaurare means to rebuild, and re- means again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 restaurare 意为重建，re- 意为再次。

items.example: Re- marks the return to a state.
items.exampleCN: re- 标记回到某种状态。
restaurare 是表示重建的动词。

items.example: Old French restorer carries the word to English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 restorer 把词带入英语。

items.example: A restorer works on old objects.

definition_en: to stop someone or something from doing something, often by holding back
core_image: 一只被绳子拉住、想冲出去却被紧紧拽住的狗
scene: 看到朋友要发火，她努力抑制自己的怒气，没有回嘴。Seeing her friend about to lose his temper, she tried to restrain her anger and said nothing back.
sceneCN: 这里 restrain 是「抑制」（第 1 个义项：克制自己的情绪或冲动）；句意：看到朋友要发火，她努力抑制自己的怒气，没有回嘴。

senses.title: Hold back a feeling
senses.definition: to control a strong feeling so that you do not act on it
senses.definitionCN: 控制强烈的情绪，不让它表现出来
senses.example: She could hardly restrain her excitement.
senses.exampleCN: 她几乎抑制不住自己的兴奋。
senses.why: The Latin source means to draw tight, so restraining an emotion is pulling it back.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为拉紧，因此抑制情绪就是把它拽回去。

senses.title: Stop someone from acting
senses.definition: to stop a person or animal from moving or doing something
senses.definitionCN: 阻止人或动物移动或做某事
senses.example: Two guards restrained the man at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 两名保安在门口拦住了那个男人。
senses.why: Physically holding someone back is the most concrete form of drawing tight.
senses.whyCN: 从身体上拉住某人，是「拉紧」最具体的形式。

senses.title: Limit an activity
senses.definition: to limit the growth or force of something
senses.definitionCN: 限制某事物的增长或力量
senses.example: High costs restrain the growth of small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 高昂的成本限制了小公司的发展。
senses.why: A force held back is a force kept within limits.
senses.whyCN: 被拉住的力，就是被限制在界限内的力。

intro.en: Restrain comes from Latin restringere, to draw tight, through Old French restreindre.
intro.cn: restrain 经古法语 restreindre 源自拉丁语 restringere（拉紧）。

items.en: Stringere means to draw tight or bind.
items.cn: stringere 意为拉紧或捆绑。

items.en: Restringere adds re- and means to hold back.
items.cn: restringere 加上 re-，意为拉住。

items.en: Restreindre keeps the sense of checking.
items.cn: restreindre 保留了抑制的含义。

items.en: Restrain covers both feelings and physical force.
items.cn: restrain 兼指情绪与身体力量。

items.en: The word also limits growth and activity.
items.cn: 这个词也用于限制增长与活动。

note.en: Restrain is close to control, restrict and hold back.
note.cn: restrain 与控制、限制、拉住等词相近。

normalIntro.en: Restrain belongs with strict: both come from the idea of drawing tight.
normalIntro.cn: restrain 与 strict 同源：两者都来自「拉紧」的想法。

normal.en: To restrain yourself is to hold your feelings on a short rope.
normal.cn: restrain yourself 就是把情绪拴在短绳上。

normal.en: Restrain anger means keep it from coming out.
normal.cn: restrain anger 意为不让怒气出来。

normal.en: A law can restrain harmful behavior.
normal.cn: 法律可以约束有害行为。

normal.en: The adjective restrained describes quiet, controlled style.
normal.cn: 形容词 restrained 描述克制含蓄的风格。

normal.en: Compare restrict: restrict sets rules, restrain pulls back force.
normal.cn: 对比 restrict：restrict 制定规则，restrain 拉住力量。

abstract.en: Picture a kite string held tight in both hands.
abstract.cn: 想象双手紧紧拉住风筝线。

abstract.en: Imagine a gate held shut against a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被人抵住，挡住人群。

abstract.en: Think of a horse stopped by a firm hand on the reins.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手稳稳拉住缰绳让马停下。

examples.en: He restrained a smile during the serious speech.
examples.cn: 在严肃的讲话中，他忍住没有笑。

examples.en: The officers restrained the crowd from entering the site.
examples.cn: 警察阻止人群进入现场。

examples.en: Several factors restrain the company from expanding too fast.
examples.cn: 几个因素限制了公司过快扩张。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）＋ strain（拉紧）」——把冲动往回拉紧，就是抑制与阻止；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ stringere（拉紧）→ restringere（拉住）→ 古法语 restreindre → restrain，核心义「往回拉住、不让冲出」。

sensesIntro.en: Restrain first holds back a feeling, then physically stops someone, and finally limits growth.
sensesIntro.cn: restrain 先指压住情绪，再指从身体上拦住某人，最后指限制增长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a taut rope stopping a dog from rushing ahead.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根绷紧的绳子拉住想冲出去的狗。

branches.en: An emotion is held back before it acts.
branches.cn: 情绪在行动之前被拉住。

branches.en: A person or animal is physically stopped.
branches.cn: 人或动物在身体上被拦住。

branches.en: Growth or force is kept within limits.
branches.cn: 增长或力量被限制在界限内。

branches.en: Holding someone back protects order.
branches.cn: 拉住某人维护了秩序。

branches.en: Physical force and social limits share the same pull.
branches.cn: 身体的力量与社会限制共享同一种拉扯。

intro.en: Restrain combines the Latin prefix re- with stringere, to draw tight.
intro.cn: restrain 由拉丁语前缀 re- 与 stringere（拉紧）组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin stringere gives strict, strain and restrain the same tight core.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stringere 让 strict、strain 与 restrain 共享「拉紧」的核心。

items.exampleCN: re- 在 restrain 中表示往回。

items.example: Old French restreindre carries the word.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 restreindre 传递了这个词。

definition_en: the quality of controlling your behavior, or something that limits action
core_image: 一双手按住桌沿，强忍着不让自己拍桌而起
scene: 面对无礼的质问，她以极大的克制保持平静，没有提高嗓门。Faced with a rude question, she showed great restraint and stayed calm without raising her voice.
sceneCN: 这里 restraint 是「克制」（第 1 个义项：控制自己的情绪与行为）；句意：面对无礼的质问，她以极大的克制保持平静，没有提高嗓门。

senses.title: Self-control
senses.definition: the ability to control your feelings or behavior
senses.definitionCN: 控制自己情绪或行为的能力
senses.example: He answered the insult with remarkable restraint.
senses.exampleCN: 面对辱骂，他以惊人的克制回应。
senses.why: The noun names the act of the verb restrain, so it is the holding back itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指动词 restrain 的行为，也就是「拉住」本身。

senses.title: A limit on action
senses.definition: a rule or condition that limits what people can do
senses.definitionCN: 限制人们行动范围的规则或条件
senses.example: The new law places restraints on advertising.
senses.exampleCN: 新法律对广告作出了限制。
senses.why: Something that holds people back is a restraint on their action.
senses.whyCN: 拉住人们的东西，就是对行动的限制。

senses.title: A physical device
senses.definition: a seat belt or other device that holds a person safely
senses.definitionCN: 安全带或其他把人固定住的装置
senses.example: The child seat has strong restraints for the shoulders.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童座椅有结实的肩部约束带。
senses.why: A belt physically restrains the body, so it is called a restraint.
senses.whyCN: 安全带在身体上拉住人，所以被称为 restraint。

intro.en: Restraint is the noun of restrain, from Latin restringere, to draw tight.
intro.cn: restraint 是 restrain 的名词形式，源自拉丁语 restringere（拉紧）。

items.en: Restringere means to hold back or bind.
items.cn: restringere 意为拉住或捆绑。

items.en: Restreindre means to check or limit.
items.cn: restreindre 意为抑制或限制。

items.en: Restraint names the act of holding back.
items.cn: restraint 指拉住的行为。

items.en: It also names rules and safety devices.
items.cn: 它也指规则与安全装置。

items.en: Wage restraint limits pay increases.
items.cn: wage restraint 限制工资上涨。

note.en: Restraint is the noun beside restrain, close to control and limit.
note.cn: restraint 是与 restrain 对应的名词，与控制和限制相近。

normalIntro.en: Restraint is what a taut rope does: it keeps force in check.
normalIntro.cn: restraint 就像绷紧的绳子：它把力量控制在范围之内。

normal.en: Show restraint means do not act on every impulse.
normal.cn: show restraint 意为不要一有冲动就行动。

normal.en: Without restraint means with no control at all.
normal.cn: without restraint 意为完全不加控制。

normal.en: A restraint on trade is a limit on business.
normal.cn: a restraint on trade 是对商业的限制。

normal.en: A seat belt is a physical restraint.
normal.cn: 安全带是一种身体约束装置。

normal.en: Compare restriction: a restraint holds back, a restriction sets rules.
normal.cn: 对比 restriction：restraint 拉住行为，restriction 制定规则。

abstract.en: Picture a hand held flat on a table to stop a fist.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手平按在桌上，压住想挥出的拳头。

abstract.en: Imagine a river held by a quiet dam.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被安静水坝拦住的河。

abstract.en: Think of a voice kept low on purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象一个故意压低的声音。

examples.en: She spoke with restraint about the painful subject.
examples.cn: 谈到这个痛苦的话题时，她说话很有克制。

examples.en: The government imposed restraints on imports.
examples.cn: 政府对进口施加了限制。

examples.en: Make sure the child seat restraints are fastened.
examples.cn: 确保儿童座椅的约束带已系好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「restrain（拉住）＋ t」——拉住的那股劲，就是克制与限制；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 restringere（拉紧）→ 古法语 restreindre → restrain ＋名词词尾 → restraint，核心义「拉住、限制的力量或状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Restraint begins as inner self-control, widens to a rule that limits action, and ends as a physical safety device.
sensesIntro.cn: restraint 从内在的自我克制，扩展到限制行动的规则，最后指身体上的安全装置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressed on a table to hold a fist back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在桌上，压住想挥出的拳头。

branches.en: The first sense is control from inside.
branches.cn: 首要义项是来自内部的自我控制。

branches.en: Rules from outside also restrain action.
branches.cn: 外部规则同样限制行动。

branches.en: A belt physically holds the body in place.
branches.cn: 安全装置在身体上把人固定住。

branches.en: A calm person and a firm rule both prevent excess.
branches.cn: 冷静的人与严格的规则都能防止过度。

branches.en: Safety devices replace self-control in a crash.
branches.cn: 发生碰撞时，安全装置接替自我控制发挥作用。

intro.en: Restraint adds a noun ending to restrain, whose root means to draw tight.
intro.cn: restraint 在 restrain 上加名词词尾，其词根意为拉紧。

latinIntro.en: Latin stringere, to draw tight, underlies the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stringere（拉紧）是整个词族的根基。

definition_en: to keep something within limits, especially by rules
core_image: 用一道栏杆把宽阔的空地围成有限的范围
scene: 为了安全，公园限制游客进入正在施工的区域。For safety, the park restricts visitors from entering the area under construction.
sceneCN: 这里 restrict 是「限制」（第 1 个义项：用规定限定范围或数量）；句意：为了安全，公园限制游客进入正在施工的区域。

senses.title: Limit an amount or area
senses.definition: to limit something such as size, amount or access
senses.definitionCN: 限制大小、数量或进入范围
senses.example: The rules restrict the number of guests.
senses.exampleCN: 规定限制了客人的数量。
senses.why: The Latin source means to draw tight, so a limit narrows what is allowed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为拉紧，因此限制就是收窄允许的范围。

senses.title: Limit freedom
senses.definition: to control what people are free to do
senses.definitionCN: 控制人们可以自由行动的范围
senses.example: Strict rules restrict what students may wear.
senses.exampleCN: 严格的规定约束了学生的穿着。
senses.why: Freedom drawn tight becomes a narrower space of action.
senses.whyCN: 自由被拉紧后，就变成了更小的行动空间。

senses.title: Keep within a range
senses.definition: to keep something inside a particular range or group
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物保持在特定范围或群体内
senses.example: Please restrict your answer to one page.
senses.exampleCN: 请把答案限定在一页之内。
senses.why: Keeping something inside a range is limiting where it may go.
senses.whyCN: 把事物保持在范围内，就是限定它可以去的地方。

intro.en: Restrict comes from Latin restrictus, the past participle of restringere, to draw tight.
intro.cn: restrict 源自拉丁语 restrictus，即 restringere（拉紧）的过去分词。

items.en: Restringere means to bind back.
items.cn: restringere 意为往回捆住。

items.en: Restrictus means drawn tight.
items.cn: restrictus 意为被拉紧的。

items.en: The participle supplies the English adjective and verb.
items.cn: 该分词提供了英语的形容词与动词。

items.en: Restrict covers rules, space and information.
items.cn: restrict 涵盖规则、空间与信息。

items.en: Restrictions appear in law and daily life.
items.cn: restriction 出现在法律与日常生活中。

note.en: Restrict is close to limit and confine, and shares a root with restrain.
note.cn: restrict 与限定、禁闭相近，并与 restrain 同源。

entries.definition: to stop something going beyond a point
to keep within a space or area

normalIntro.en: Restrict shares its tight root with strict: strict rules restrict what we do.
normalIntro.cn: restrict 与 strict 共享「拉紧」的词根：严格的规定限制我们的行为。

normal.en: Restrict access means fewer people may enter.
normal.cn: restrict access 意为更少的人可以进入。

normal.en: Restrict someone to a place means keep them there.
normal.cn: restrict someone to a place 意为把人限制在某处。

normal.en: The rules restrict freedom of movement.
normal.cn: 这些规定限制行动自由。

normal.en: The noun restriction is the limit itself.
normal.cn: 名词 restriction 就是限制本身。

normal.en: Compare restrain: restrain pulls back a force, restrict draws a boundary.
normal.cn: 对比 restrain：restrain 拉住力量，restrict 画出边界。

abstract.en: Picture a wide field narrowed by a fence.
abstract.cn: 想象一片宽阔的田地被人用围栏圈窄。

abstract.en: Imagine a door that opens only for a few people.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇只为少数人打开的门。

abstract.en: Think of a page with only one small writing space.
abstract.cn: 想象一页只留出小小一块书写空间。

examples.en: Doctors restrict the use of this drug to adults.
examples.cn: 医生把这种药的使用限定在成人范围内。

examples.en: The city restricts traffic in the old town.
examples.cn: 该市限制老城区的交通。

examples.en: He restricts himself to one cup of coffee a day.
examples.cn: 他限定自己每天只喝一杯咖啡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）＋ strict（严格）」——用严格的规定把范围往回收紧，就是限制；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ stringere（拉紧）→ restrictus（被拉紧的）→ restrict，核心义「把范围收紧、划定边界」。

sensesIntro.en: Restrict first limits an amount or area, then limits freedom, and finally keeps something within a range.
sensesIntro.cn: restrict 先指限制数量或范围，再指约束自由，最后指把事物限定在某个区间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fence turning open ground into a small enclosure.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道围栏把开阔的空地围成小小的圈。

branches.en: Amount and access are the first things limited.
branches.cn: 数量与进入权限是最先被限制的对象。

branches.en: Rules also narrow personal freedom.
branches.cn: 规则也缩小个人自由。

branches.en: Something is kept inside a chosen range.
branches.cn: 事物被保持在选定的范围内。

branches.en: Limiting access is a common form of controlling freedom.
branches.cn: 限制进入是控制自由的常见方式。

branches.en: A range of action is a kind of small freedom.
branches.cn: 行动范围就是一种有限的自由。

intro.en: Restrict is built on Latin strictus, drawn tight, with the prefix re-.
intro.cn: restrict 建立在拉丁语 strictus（被拉紧的）之上，并带前缀 re-。

latinIntro.en: Latin stringere gives the family its tight core: strict, strain, restrict.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stringere 赋予词族「拉紧」的核心：strict、strain、restrict。

items.example: Strict keeps the same tight idea.
items.exampleCN: strict 保留同样的拉紧含义。
restrictive 描述限制性的规则。

definition_en: a rule or condition that limits what people can do
core_image: 一条画在地上的界线，把可以走的地方收窄
scene: 图书馆对借书数量有严格限制，每人一次只能借五本。The library has a strict restriction on borrowing: each person may take only five books at a time.
sceneCN: 这里 restriction 是「限制规定」（第 2 个义项：明确规定范围或数量的规则）；句意：图书馆对借书数量有严格限制，每人一次只能借五本。

senses.title: A limit on action
senses.definition: a limit on what someone can do or have
senses.definitionCN: 对某人能做或能拥有之事的限定
senses.example: The restriction on water use lasted all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 用水限制持续了整个夏天。
senses.why: The noun names the result of restricting, so it is the limit itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词表示 restricting 的结果，因此就是限制本身。

senses.title: An official rule
senses.definition: an official rule that says what is not allowed
senses.definitionCN: 规定什么不被允许的正式规则
senses.example: New restrictions cover food imports.
senses.exampleCN: 新的限制规定涉及食品进口。
senses.why: A limit written down and enforced becomes a rule.
senses.whyCN: 被写下来并执行的限制，就成了规定。

senses.title: The act of limiting
senses.definition: the act of keeping something within limits
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物保持在界限内的行为
senses.example: The restriction of free speech raises hard questions.
senses.exampleCN: 对言论自由的限定引出了棘手的问题。
senses.why: Restriction can name the process as well as its result.
senses.whyCN: restriction 既能指结果，也能指过程。

intro.en: Restriction adds -ion to restrict, from Latin restrictus, drawn tight.
intro.cn: restriction 在 restrict 上加 -ion，源自拉丁语 restrictus（被拉紧的）。

items.en: Restringere means to draw tight.
items.cn: restringere 意为拉紧。

items.en: Restrictus means drawn tight.
items.cn: restrictus 意为被拉紧的。

items.en: Restrict enters English as a verb.
items.cn: restrict 作为动词进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ion forms the noun restriction.
items.cn: 后缀 -ion 构成名词 restriction。

items.en: Restrictions now appear in law, travel and trade.
items.cn: restriction 如今出现在法律、旅行与贸易中。

note.en: Restriction is the noun of restrict and is close to limit and rule.
note.cn: restriction 是 restrict 的名词，与限定和规则相近。

normalIntro.en: Restriction is the noun of restrict: the boundary that has been drawn tight.
normalIntro.cn: restriction 是 restrict 的名词：那条被收紧的边界。

normal.en: Impose restrictions means put limits in place.
normal.cn: impose restrictions 意为施加限制。

normal.en: Lift restrictions means remove the limits.
normal.cn: lift restrictions 意为解除限制。

normal.en: Travel restrictions control where people may go.
normal.cn: travel restrictions 控制人们可以去哪里。

normal.en: Without restriction means with no limit at all.
normal.cn: without restriction 意为完全不受限制。

normal.en: Compare restraint: a restraint is a pull, a restriction is a rule.
normal.cn: 对比 restraint：restraint 是拉住的力量，restriction 是规则。

abstract.en: Picture a line on the floor that nobody may cross.
abstract.cn: 想象地上一条谁也不许越过的线。

abstract.en: Imagine a sign that lists what is not allowed.
abstract.cn: 想象一块列出禁止事项的牌子。

abstract.en: Think of a door narrowed so only one person fits.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇被改窄、只能容一人通过的门。

examples.en: The city put restrictions on new building heights.
examples.cn: 该市对新建筑的高度施加了限制。

examples.en: There are restrictions on taking photos inside.
examples.cn: 馆内拍照有规定限制。

examples.en: The restriction of movement helped stop the spread.
examples.cn: 对人员流动的限定帮助阻止了扩散。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「restrict（限制）＋ ion」——把范围收紧之后留下的那条界线，就是限制规定；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ stringere（拉紧）→ restrictus（被拉紧的）→ restrict ＋ -ion → restriction，核心义「被收紧的范围或规则」。

sensesIntro.en: Restriction first names a limit, then an official rule, and finally the act of limiting itself.
sensesIntro.cn: restriction 先指限制，再指正式规定，最后指限定这一行为本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line on the ground narrowing the allowed space.
core.cn: 核心意象：地上一条把允许空间收窄的界线。

branches.en: The basic sense is a limit on what may be done.
branches.cn: 基本义是对可以做什么的限定。

branches.en: A written limit becomes an official rule.
branches.cn: 写下来的限定成为正式规定。

branches.en: The word also names the limiting process.
branches.cn: 这个词也指限制的过程。

branches.en: Rules give everyday limits their force.
branches.cn: 规则赋予日常限制以效力。

branches.en: Enforcing a rule is the act of restricting.
branches.cn: 执行规则就是限制的行为。

intro.en: Restriction adds the noun suffix -ion to restrict, whose root means drawn tight.
intro.cn: restriction 在 restrict 后加名词后缀 -ion，其词根意为拉紧。

latinIntro.en: Latin strictus, drawn tight, underlies restrict and restriction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 strictus（被拉紧的）是 restrict 与 restriction 的根基。

items.exampleCN: restricted 描述受限的进入权限。

definition_en: something that happens because of an action, event or process
core_image: 石子落入水中，一圈圈波纹向外扩散开来
scene: 连续熬夜之后，他在体检中得到了一个令人担忧的结果。After several late nights, he received a worrying result in his medical check.
sceneCN: 这里 result 是「结果」（第 1 个义项：某个过程或行动带来的结局）；句意：连续熬夜之后，他在体检中得到了一个令人担忧的结果。

senses.title: An outcome
senses.definition: something that happens because of something else
senses.definitionCN: 因其他事物而发生的结果
senses.example: The accident was the result of careless driving.
senses.exampleCN: 这场事故是粗心驾驶的结果。
senses.why: The Latin source means to spring back, and an outcome springs from its cause.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为弹回，而结果正是从原因中弹出来的。

senses.title: A score or grade
senses.definition: the score or mark achieved in a test or competition
senses.definitionCN: 在考试或比赛中取得的分数或名次
senses.example: Her exam results were the best in the class.
senses.exampleCN: 她的考试成绩是班里最好的。
senses.why: A score is the measured outcome of effort in a test.
senses.whyCN: 分数就是考试努力被测量出来的结果。

senses.title: To cause something
senses.definition: to happen as a consequence, usually with in or from
senses.definitionCN: 作为后果而发生，通常与 in 或 from 连用
senses.example: The delay resulted in a missed flight.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误导致错过了航班。
senses.why: As a verb, the word points from a cause to whatever it brings about.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时，这个词从原因指向它所带来的一切。

intro.en: Result comes from Latin resultare, to spring back, through French resulter.
intro.cn: result 经法语 resulter 源自拉丁语 resultare（弹回）。

items.en: Saltare means to leap.
items.cn: saltare 意为跳跃。

items.en: Resultare means to spring back.
items.cn: resultare 意为弹回。

items.en: Resulter carries the sense of following from something.
items.cn: resulter 带有「由某事物而来」的含义。

items.en: Result names the outcome that follows a cause.
items.cn: result 指随原因而来的结果。

items.en: The verb result in marks a consequence.
items.cn: 动词短语 result in 标记一种后果。

note.en: Result is close to effect and consequence and pairs with cause.
note.cn: result 与 effect、consequence 相近，并与 cause 相对。

entries.definition: the final result of a process

normalIntro.en: Result is what springs back from a cause, like ripples from a stone.
normalIntro.cn: result 是原因弹回来的东西，就像石子激起的涟漪。

normal.en: As a result means because of what happened.
normal.cn: as a result 意为由于所发生的事。

normal.en: Result in points forward to the effect.
normal.cn: result in 指向后来的结果。

normal.en: Result from points back to the cause.
normal.cn: result from 指向前面的原因。

normal.en: Exam results are measured outcomes.
normal.cn: exam results 是被测量出来的成绩。

normal.en: Compare outcome: a result is immediate, an outcome is the final end.
normal.cn: 对比 outcome：result 较直接，outcome 是最终结局。

abstract.en: Picture a stone dropping and rings spreading out.
abstract.cn: 想象石子落下，一圈圈波纹扩散。

abstract.en: Imagine a ball bouncing back from a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象球从墙上弹回。

abstract.en: Think of a seed that finally shows as a flower.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子最终开成花。

examples.en: The result of the vote surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 投票结果让所有人吃惊。

examples.en: She checked her results online.
examples.cn: 她在网上查询了自己的成绩。

examples.en: Heavy rain resulted in the game being canceled.
examples.cn: 大雨导致比赛取消。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）＋ sult（跳）」——事情做完后弹回来的东西，就是结果；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ saltare（跳）→ resultare（弹回）→ 法语 resulter → result，核心义「从原因中弹回来的结局」。

sensesIntro.en: Result first names an outcome, then a test score, and as a verb it points to what a cause brings about.
sensesIntro.cn: result 先指结果，再指考试成绩，作动词时指原因所带来的一切。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ripples spreading from a stone dropped in water.
core.cn: 核心意象：石子入水后向外扩散的波纹。

branches.en: The basic sense is whatever follows from a cause.
branches.cn: 基本义是随原因而来的一切。

branches.en: A score is the measured result of effort.
branches.cn: 分数是努力被测量出的结果。

branches.en: The verb links a cause to its consequence.
branches.cn: 动词把原因与后果连接起来。

branches.en: Exam results are a familiar kind of outcome.
branches.cn: 考试成绩是常见的一类结果。

branches.en: Every result has a cause behind it.
branches.cn: 每个结果背后都有原因。

intro.en: Result is built from re- and Latin saltare, to leap.
intro.cn: result 由 re- 与拉丁语 saltare（跳）构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin resultare means to spring back, like a ball from a wall.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 resultare 意为弹回，如同球从墙上弹回。

items.exampleCN: 法语 resulter 传递了该词。
resulting 描述随之而来的事物。

definition_zh: 重新开始；恢复；重新取得
definition_en: to begin again after a pause, or to take back a position
core_image: 停下的钟摆被人轻轻一推，又重新摆动起来
scene: 雨停之后，工人们重新开始修建那条小路。After the rain stopped, the workers resumed building the path.
sceneCN: 这里 resume 是「重新开始」（第 1 个义项：停顿之后再次进行）；句意：雨停之后，工人们重新开始修建那条小路。

pos.zh: 重新开始；恢复；重新取得

senses.title: Begin again
senses.definition: to start something again after a break
senses.definitionCN: 在停顿之后再次开始某事
senses.example: The meeting will resume after lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 会议将在午餐后重新开始。
senses.why: The Latin source means to take up again, so resuming picks an activity back up.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为重新拿起，因此 resume 就是把活动重新拾起。

senses.title: Take back a position
senses.definition: to return to an office, seat or duty
senses.definitionCN: 回到职位、座位或职责上
senses.example: She resumed her duties as manager in May.
senses.exampleCN: 她在五月重新履行经理职责。
senses.why: Taking up a role again is the same gesture of picking something back up.
senses.whyCN: 重新担任职务，同样是「重新拿起」的动作。

intro.en: Resume comes from Latin resumere, to take up again, from sumere, to take.
intro.cn: resume 源自拉丁语 resumere（重新拿起），由 sumere（拿）构成。

items.en: Sumere means to take up.
items.cn: sumere 意为拿起。

items.en: Resumere means to take up again.
items.cn: resumere 意为重新拿起。

items.en: Resumer keeps the sense of continuing.
items.cn: resumer 保留了继续的含义。

items.en: Resume means begin again after stopping.
items.cn: resume 意为停下后重新开始。

items.en: It also means return to an office or duty.
items.cn: 它也指回到职位或职责。

note.en: Resume is close to continue and restart, and is not the noun for a CV.
note.cn: resume 与 continue、restart 相近，注意它不是指简历的名词。

entries.definition: to begin something again with new energy

normalIntro.en: Resume is re- plus sume, take: take the activity up again.
normalIntro.cn: resume 是 re- 加 sume（拿）：把活动重新拿起来。

normal.en: Resume work means start working again after a break.
normal.cn: resume work 意为休息后重新工作。

normal.en: Resume talks means bring the talks back to life.
normal.cn: resume talks 意为让谈判重新进行。

normal.en: Resume one's seat means sit down again.
normal.cn: resume one's seat 意为重新坐下。

normal.en: The noun resumption names the fresh start.
normal.cn: 名词 resumption 指重新开始。

normal.en: Keep resume apart from the CV spelled with accents.
normal.cn: 注意把 resume 与带重音符号的简历一词区分开。

abstract.en: Picture a paused clock starting to tick again.
abstract.cn: 想象一只停下的钟重新滴答走动。

abstract.en: Imagine a book reopened at the exact page.
abstract.cn: 想象一本书正好在原来那页重新打开。

abstract.en: Think of a runner who stumbles and then sets off again.
abstract.cn: 想象跑步者踉跄一下后又重新起跑。

examples.en: Negotiations resumed after a short pause.
examples.cn: 短暂停顿后谈判重新开始。

examples.en: He resumed his seat at the head of the table.
examples.cn: 他重新坐回桌子主位。

examples.en: The team hopes to resume training next week.
examples.cn: 球队希望下周恢复训练。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）＋ sume（拿起）」——把放下的事重新拿起来，就是重新开始；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再）＋ sumere（拿）→ resumere（重新拿起）→ 法语 resumer → resume，核心义「把停下的活动重新拿起」。

sensesIntro.en: Resume first means begin again after a break, and then return to a position or duty.
sensesIntro.cn: resume 先指停顿后重新开始，再指回到职位或职责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stopped pendulum pushed back into motion.
core.cn: 核心意象：停下的钟摆被推一下又重新摆动。

branches.en: An activity starts again after a gap.
branches.cn: 活动在间隔之后再次开始。

branches.en: A person returns to an office or duty.
branches.cn: 人回到职位或职责上。

branches.en: Returning to work is both a fresh start and a return.
branches.cn: 重返工作是重新开始，也是回归。

branches.en: Talks and work are the most common objects.
branches.cn: 谈判与工作是最常见的宾语。

branches.en: Royalty and officials also resume duties.
branches.cn: 王室成员与官员也会恢复职责。

intro.en: Resume is re- plus sumere, to take, with a French spelling in between.
intro.cn: resume 由 re- 与 sumere（拿）构成，中间经过法语拼写。

latinIntro.en: Latin sumere means to take up; resumere means to take up again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sumere 意为拿起；resumere 意为重新拿起。

items.exampleCN: 法语 resumer 传递了该词。

items.example: Resumable describes a task that can pause and restart.
items.exampleCN: resumable 描述可暂停再继续的任务。

definition_en: to keep something or continue to have it
core_image: 一只手紧紧握住一件东西，不肯松开
scene: 这家老店保留了许多传统做法，连包装纸都没有换过。The old shop retains many traditional methods, and even its wrapping paper has never changed.
sceneCN: 这里 retain 是「保留」（第 1 个义项：继续拥有、不放弃）；句意：这家老店保留了许多传统做法，连包装纸都没有换过。

senses.title: Keep possession
senses.definition: to keep something and not give it away or lose it
senses.definitionCN: 保留某物，不送走也不丢失
senses.example: The museum retains the right to refuse entry.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆保留拒绝入场的权利。
senses.why: The Latin source means to hold back, so retaining is keeping a hold on something.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为握住，因此 retain 就是继续握住某物。

senses.title: Continue to have a quality
senses.definition: to continue to have a quality or condition
senses.definitionCN: 继续具有某种性质或状态
senses.example: Thick walls retain heat in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 厚墙在冬天能保持热量。
senses.why: A quality that stays with an object is held in place, as if by a hand.
senses.whyCN: 留在物体上的性质就像被一只手按在原地。

senses.title: Remember information
senses.definition: to keep facts in your memory
senses.definitionCN: 把事实保存在记忆中
senses.example: Students retain more when they review often.
senses.exampleCN: 经常复习的学生记得更牢。
senses.why: Memory holds information the way a hand holds an object.
senses.whyCN: 记忆保存信息，就像手握住物品一样。

intro.en: Retain comes from Latin retinere, to hold back, from tenere, to hold.
intro.cn: retain 源自拉丁语 retinere（握住），由 tenere（握）构成。

items.en: Tenere means to hold.
items.cn: tenere 意为握住。

items.en: Retinere means to hold back or keep.
items.cn: retinere 意为拉住或保留。

items.en: Retenir keeps the sense of keeping.
items.cn: retenir 保留了「保留」的含义。

items.en: Retain means keep in possession.
items.cn: retain 意为继续拥有。

items.en: It also covers heat, memory and employees.
items.cn: 它也用于热量、记忆与员工。

note.en: Retain is close to keep and preserve, and shares a root with contain.
note.cn: retain 与保持、保存相近，并与 contain 同根。

entries.definition: to keep something in good condition
to keep something at the same level

normalIntro.en: Retain is re- plus tain, hold: keep holding on.
normalIntro.cn: retain 是 re- 加 tain（握）：一直握着不放。

normal.en: Retain control means do not let go of power.
normal.cn: retain control 意为不放松权力。

normal.en: Retain information means keep it in memory.
normal.cn: retain information 意为把信息留在记忆里。

normal.en: Thick walls retain heat well.
normal.cn: 厚墙能很好地保温。

normal.en: Companies try to retain good staff.
normal.cn: 公司努力留住优秀员工。

normal.en: Compare maintain: maintain keeps a level, retain keeps possession.
normal.cn: 对比 maintain：maintain 保持水平，retain 保持拥有。

abstract.en: Picture a fist closed around a smooth stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手紧紧攥住一块光滑的石头。

abstract.en: Imagine warmth staying inside a wool coat.
abstract.cn: 想象温暖留在羊毛大衣里。

abstract.en: Think of a name written firmly in memory.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被牢牢写进记忆。

examples.en: The company retained its best engineers.
examples.cn: 公司留住了最优秀的工程师。

examples.en: Dark surfaces retain more heat than light ones.
examples.cn: 深色表面比浅色表面能保留更多热量。

examples.en: Few people retain every detail of a lecture.
examples.cn: 很少有人能记住讲座的每个细节。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（一直）＋ tain（握住）」——一直握住不放，就是保留与保持；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回、持续）＋ tenere（握）→ retinere（握住不放）→ 法语 retenir → retain，核心义「继续握住、不失去」。

sensesIntro.en: Retain first means keep possession, then keep a quality, and finally keep information in memory.
sensesIntro.cn: retain 先指保留拥有，再指保持性质，最后指把信息留在记忆中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closed tight around something it will not release.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手紧紧攥住不肯松开的东西。

branches.en: Possession is the basic sense of keeping.
branches.cn: 拥有是「保留」的基本义。

branches.en: A quality stays in place like heat in a wall.
branches.cn: 性质留在原处，如同墙中的热量。

branches.en: Memory holds facts the way a hand holds objects.
branches.cn: 记忆保存事实，如同手握物品。

branches.en: Keeping an object often keeps its value too.
branches.cn: 保留物品往往也保住了它的价值。

branches.en: A retentive mind keeps what it learns.
branches.cn: 记性好的头脑能留住所学。

intro.en: Retain joins re- with Latin tenere, to hold.
intro.cn: retain 由 re- 与拉丁语 tenere（握）组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin tenere, to hold, also gives contain, maintain and detain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tenere（握）也构成 contain、maintain 与 detain。

items.exampleCN: tenere 是表示握住的动词。
法语 retenir 传递了该词。
retentive 描述很强的记忆力。

definition_en: to stop working because of age, or to move away to a quiet place
core_image: 一位老人合上办公室的门，慢慢走向安静的院子
scene: 在这所学校教了三十年书后，她今年夏天退休了。After teaching at this school for thirty years, she retired this summer.
sceneCN: 这里 retire 是「退休」（第 1 个义项：因年龄原因停止工作）；句意：在这所学校教了三十年书后，她今年夏天退休了。

senses.title: Stop working
senses.definition: to leave your job because you have reached a certain age
senses.definitionCN: 因达到一定年龄而离开工作岗位
senses.example: My father retired at sixty.
senses.exampleCN: 我父亲六十岁退休。
senses.why: The French source means to withdraw, so retiring is stepping back from work.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源意为撤退，因此退休就是从工作中退下来。

senses.title: Leave a sport or service
senses.definition: to stop taking part in a sport or leave military service
senses.definitionCN: 停止参加体育运动或离开军队服役
senses.example: The champion retired from tennis last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这位冠军去年从网坛退役。
senses.why: Leaving a public career is another form of withdrawing.
senses.whyCN: 离开公开的职业生涯，是另一种撤退。

senses.title: Withdraw to rest
senses.definition: to go away to a quiet place, especially to rest or sleep
senses.definitionCN: 到一个安静的地方去，尤其是休息或睡觉
senses.example: The guests retired to their rooms after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后客人们各自回房休息。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply to draw back, which survives in formal use.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义就是「退回」，这一用法在正式语境中保留下来。

intro.en: Retire comes from French retirer, to draw back, from tirer, to pull.
intro.cn: retire 源自法语 retirer（退回），由 tirer（拉）构成。

items.en: Tirer means to pull or draw.
items.cn: tirer 意为拉或拖。

items.en: Retirer means to draw back.
items.cn: retirer 意向往后撤。

items.en: Retire first means withdraw to a private place.
items.cn: retire 最初指退到私密之处。

items.en: The word comes to mean leaving work at a certain age.
items.cn: 这个词后来指到一定年龄离开工作。

items.en: Athletes also retire from competition.
items.cn: 运动员也会从比赛中退役。

note.en: Retire is close to withdraw and resign, but implies age or long service.
note.cn: retire 与撤退、辞职相近，但强调年龄或长期服务。

entries.definition: to move away from a place or activity

normalIntro.en: Retire is re- plus tire, pull: pull yourself back from work.
normalIntro.cn: retire 是 re- 加 tire（拉）：把自己从工作中拉回来。

normal.en: Retire from work means leave your job for good.
normal.cn: retire from work 意为永久离开工作。

normal.en: Retire early means stop working sooner than usual.
normal.cn: retire early 意为比通常更早停止工作。

normal.en: Soldiers retire from the army.
normal.cn: 军人从军队退役。

normal.en: Retire to bed is a formal way to say go to sleep.
normal.cn: retire to bed 是「就寝」的正式说法。

normal.en: Compare resign: resign is a choice at any age, retire usually follows long service.
normal.cn: 对比 resign：resign 任何年龄都可主动辞职，retire 通常指长期服务后退休。

abstract.en: Picture a door closing softly on a long career.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门在漫长职业生涯后轻轻合上。

abstract.en: Imagine an armchair waiting by a quiet window.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子在安静的窗边等候。

abstract.en: Think of an athlete laying down a racket for the last time.
abstract.cn: 想象运动员最后一次放下球拍。

examples.en: She plans to retire next spring.
examples.cn: 她计划明年春天退休。

examples.en: The general retired after forty years of service.
examples.cn: 这位将军服役四十年后退役。

examples.en: We retired to the garden when the sun went down.
examples.cn: 太阳落山后，我们退到花园里休息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）＋ tire（拉）」——把一直往前奔的自己往回拉，就是退下来、退休；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 法语 re-（回）＋ tirer（拉）→ retirer（退回）→ retire，核心义「从工作或人群中退回来」。

sensesIntro.en: Retire first means leave work at a certain age, then leave a sport or service, and finally withdraw to rest.
sensesIntro.cn: retire 先指到龄离开工作，再指从运动或军旅中退出，最后指退下休息。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: closing an office door and walking toward a quiet yard.
core.cn: 核心意象：合上办公室的门，走向安静的院子。

branches.en: Leaving a job at a certain age is the main sense.
branches.cn: 到龄离开工作是主要义项。

branches.en: Athletes and soldiers also retire.
branches.cn: 运动员和军人也会退役。

branches.en: The old sense of withdrawing survives in formal speech.
branches.cn: 「退回」的古老含义在正式语言中保留。

branches.en: Retiring from work is a withdrawal into private life.
branches.cn: 从工作退休就是退回私人生活。

branches.en: A retired athlete steps back from public competition.
branches.cn: 退役运动员从公开赛事中退下。

intro.en: Retire has a French shape: re- plus tirer, to pull.
intro.cn: retire 带着法语形态：re- 加 tirer（拉）。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root here; the word comes through French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语词根，是经法语传入的。

items.example: Retired describes a person who has left work.
items.exampleCN: retired 描述已经离开工作的人。

items.example: A retiree has left work for good.
items.exampleCN: retiree 指永久离开工作的人。
